plan: My private value is $30. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This means bidding $30 protects my potential profit margin. If I bid less, I risk losing the item when I would have profited. If I bid more, I risk paying more than my value. With no previous round history and independent value drawing, a true-value bid is most rational.

My private value is $7. In a second-price sealed bid auction, my optimal strategy is to bid my true value when I'm uncertain about other bidders' valuations. Since the values are randomly drawn and this is a one-round game, I'll bid close to my actual value. Bidding exactly $7 reveals my true willingness to pay and minimizes the risk of overbidding. This strategy balances potential profit with avoiding overpaying.

My private value is $36, which means I want to maximize my potential profit. Since values are independently drawn, I'll aim to bid strategically. A good approach is to bid close to, but slightly below my true value. This allows me to potentially win if others bid lower, while protecting against overpaying.
